assessment.headline: OpenAI's downsized $11B close and Oracle's costly $20B raise keep AI financing stress elevated.
assessment.digest_markdown:
**What changed this week**

- **Markets wobbled.** The Nasdaq-100 is down about 13% in four weeks, and the VIX jumped to 28 on Nov 5.
- **Credit spreads widened.** High-yield spreads rose to 3.48%, from 3.15% four weeks ago.

**AI financing is getting harder and pricier, but it is not drying up.**

- **OpenAI** closed about $11B at a $1.25T valuation (Bloomberg). Reports say the round target was cut by $10B and some backers trimmed their allocations.
- **Oracle** raised $20B. Half came from bonds yielding 7-8.65% and half from stock sold at an 11.2% discount. Its default-insurance cost (CDS) is quoted at roughly 263-300bp; CNBC's figure is 295bp.
- **CoreWeave** bonds slid further, to about 77.50 per aggregator data.
- **The bright spot:** Microsoft's $25B bond drew $115B of orders.

**Real spending still looks strong.**

- Hyperscaler capex rose 27% quarter on quarter in the latest filings.
- Signed-but-not-started leases grew another 20%.
- AMD guided data-center revenue up 50% next quarter.
- Foxconn's October sales rose 46% year on year.
- **The catch:** Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Oracle all had negative free cash flow, so more of the build-out now runs on debt.

**Local pushback is growing.** San Diego and Charlotte have moratoriums, and restrictions now reach 42 states. So far, announcements keep rising anyway.

**Why it matters:** The usual warning sign before a capex slowdown is financing stress. That stress is visible now, concentrated in Oracle, CoreWeave and OpenAI, while suppliers still report booming demand.

**What to watch next**

- CoreWeave's results on Nov 10.
- Whether OpenAI's round reaches $20B.
- How Oracle's new bonds trade.

Note: Nvidia, TSMC and memory makers were not checked this week. Not investment advice.
